questions.question: What are trophic levels? Give an example of a food chain and state the different trophic levels in it.
answer_steps: The various steps in a food chain, at which energy is transferred, are trophic levels.
Example: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake.
Grass: producer (first level); grasshopper: primary consumer (second); frog: secondary consumer (third); snake: tertiary consumer (fourth).

questions.question: What is the role of decomposers in the ecosystem?
answer_steps: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down the dead remains and wastes of organisms into simple substances.
These substances go back into the soil and are used again by plants: decomposers recycle nutrients and keep the environment clean.

questions.question: Why are some substances biodegradable and some non-biodegradable?
answer_steps: Microorganisms break down substances using enzymes, and enzymes are specific: each acts only on certain substances.
Natural materials (peels, paper) can be broken down; many synthetic materials (plastics, DDT) cannot, so they are non-biodegradable.

questions.question: Give any two ways in which biodegradable substances would affect the environment.
answer_steps: In large amounts they rot, give a foul smell and breed flies and germs that spread disease.
Their decomposition can release gases such as methane and carbon dioxide; if properly composted, they enrich the soil.

questions.question: Give any two ways in which non-biodegradable substances would affect the environment.
answer_steps: They remain for a very long time and pile up, polluting soil and water and blocking drains.
Animals may swallow plastics and die, and toxic chemicals can enter food chains and undergo biological magnification.

questions.question: What is ozone and how does it affect any ecosystem?
answer_steps: Ozone (O₃) is a molecule of three oxygen atoms. At ground level it is a deadly poison.
High in the atmosphere, the ozone layer shields the earth from the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation.
If it is depleted, more UV reaches the earth, causing skin cancer and damage to plants, animals and the whole ecosystem.

questions.question: How can you help in reducing the problem of waste disposal? Give any two methods.
answer_steps: Separate wet (biodegradable) and dry (non-biodegradable) waste, and compost kitchen waste.
Carry cloth bags, avoid single-use plastic, and reuse and recycle things wherever possible.

questions.question: Which of the following groups contain only biodegradable items?
questions.explanation: Cake, wood and grass are all broken down by decomposers. (Option (c) is also biodegradable; the NCERT answer is (d).)
option_feedback: Leather takes very long to break down and is usually treated.
These are biodegradable too; the NCERT answer is (d), but (c) is also acceptable.

questions.question: Which of the following constitute a food-chain?
questions.explanation: Grass (producer) → goat (herbivore) → human (consumer).
option_feedback: These are all herbivores; there is no producer.
A goat does not eat fish.

options: Carrying cloth-bags to put purchases in while shopping
Switching off unnecessary lights and fans
Walking to school instead of getting your mother to drop you on her scooter
questions.explanation: Each of these reduces waste or saves energy.
option_feedback: True, but the others are also eco-friendly.
True, but the others are also eco-friendly.
True, but the others are also eco-friendly.

questions.question: What will happen if we kill all the organisms in one trophic level?
answer_steps: The organisms of the next trophic level would lose their food and decline or die.
The organisms of the level below would increase without control. The food chain breaks and the balance of the ecosystem is disturbed.

questions.question: Will the impact of removing all the organisms in a trophic level be different for different trophic levels? Can the organisms of any trophic level be removed without causing any damage to the ecosystem?
answer_steps: Yes, the impact differs. Removing producers would remove the food and energy for every other level, and the whole ecosystem would collapse.
Removing a consumer level would let the level below multiply and starve the level above; removing decomposers would stop the recycling of nutrients and let dead matter pile up.
No trophic level can be removed without causing damage, because all levels are linked.

questions.question: What is biological magnification? Will the levels of this magnification be different at different levels of the ecosystem?
answer_steps: The increase in concentration of non-degradable harmful chemicals (such as pesticides) at successive trophic levels is biological magnification.
Yes: the concentration is lowest at the producer level and highest at the top consumer level.

questions.question: What are the problems caused by the non-biodegradable wastes that we generate?
answer_steps: They do not break down, so they pile up as heaps of garbage and occupy land.
They pollute soil and water; plastics block drains and harm animals that swallow them.
Toxic chemicals from them enter food chains and undergo biological magnification, harming humans.

questions.question: If all the waste we generate is biodegradable, will this have no impact on the environment?
answer_steps: It will still have an impact: large amounts of biodegradable waste rot, give a foul smell and spread disease.
Decomposition also releases gases such as methane; the waste must be managed, for example by composting.

questions.question:
Which are the correct statements related to ozone?

(i) Ozone layer helps in increasing the UV radiations reaching earth.

(ii) Ozone is a deadly poison.

(iii) Ozone layer shields the earth from UV radiations.

(iv) Ozone layer prevents UV rays which cause skin cancer.

(v) Ozone is formed with the help of Chloroflurocarbons.
questions.explanation: Ozone is a poison at ground level and shields the earth from UV; it does not increase UV, and CFCs destroy it rather than form it.
option_feedback: Statement (i) is wrong: ozone reduces UV.
Statement (v) is wrong: CFCs destroy ozone.

questions.question: Which of the following human activities has resulted in an increase of non-biodegradable substances?
options: Use of plastic as packaging material
questions.explanation: Plastic packaging is non-biodegradable.

Check the Assertion again: it is false, because the vulture, at the top, has the most pesticide.
Check the Assertion again: it is false, because the vulture, at the top, has the most pesticide.

questions.question:
About 100 acres of forest land was declared as Natural reserve park. The following organisms were predominant in the Natural reserve park: rabbit, frog, grass, fish, fox, water insects, zebra, peacock, snake, trees, bird, owl, insects, tiger, vulture, duck.

Create a food web comprising two separate food chains with different producers by using the above data.
answer_steps: Tree food chain: trees → zebra → tiger (any other correct chain).
Grassland food chain: grass → zebra → tiger. Join the two chains at the common point, zebra, to make a food web.

questions.question: Match the trophic level with the type of consumer: 2nd trophic level
questions.explanation: The second level is herbivores: primary consumers.

questions.question: Match the trophic level with the type of consumer: 3rd trophic level
questions.explanation: The third level is small carnivores: secondary consumers.

questions.question: Write the differences between biotic factor and abiotic factor.
answer_steps: Biotic factors are the living components of an ecosystem: plants, animals and microorganisms.
Abiotic factors are the non-living components: temperature, rainfall, wind, soil and minerals.

questions.question: Write a note on biological magnification.
answer_steps: Non-degradable chemicals such as pesticides enter food chains through soil and water and are not broken down in the body.
Their concentration increases at each trophic level; humans at the top collect the most.

questions.question:
(a) Explain the formation of ozone with equations.

(b) How can you help in reducing the problem of waste disposal? Write two methods.
answer_steps: (a) Ultraviolet radiation splits oxygen molecules into free oxygen atoms: $\mathrm{O_{2} \rightarrow O + O}$
The oxygen atoms combine with oxygen molecules to form ozone: $\mathrm{O + O_{2} \rightarrow O_{3}}$
(b) Separate wet and dry waste and compost the wet waste; carry cloth bags and avoid single-use plastic.

questions.question: The organisms which prepare their own food are called ____.
questions.explanation: Green plants make their own food: producers.

questions.question: The organisms which feed on plants are called ____.
questions.explanation: Plant eaters are herbivores.

questions.question: How can you help in reducing the problem of waste disposal? Give any two methods.
answer_steps: Separate wet and dry waste, and compost kitchen waste at home.
Use cloth bags and reusable containers instead of plastic, and send paper, glass and metal for recycling.

questions.question: Classify the following ecosystems into natural ecosystem and artificial ecosystems: Forest, garden, aquarium, sea
answer_steps: Natural ecosystems: forest, sea.
Artificial ecosystems: garden, aquarium.

questions.question: Which of these is an abiotic component of an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Temperature is non-living.

questions.question: Decomposers are mainly:
questions.explanation: Bacteria and fungi break down dead remains.

questions.question: Green plants capture about what percentage of the sunlight falling on their leaves?
questions.explanation: Only about 1% is converted into food energy.
option_feedback: 10% is what passes between trophic levels.

questions.question: If producers have 1000 J of energy, the secondary consumers get about:
questions.explanation: 1000 → 100 (primary) → 10 J (secondary).

questions.question: The flow of energy in an ecosystem is:
questions.explanation: Energy passes one way: Sun → producers → consumers; it does not return.

questions.question: In the food chain grass → deer → lion, the deer is a:
questions.explanation: The deer eats plants: herbivore, primary consumer.

questions.question: The chemicals mainly responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer are:
questions.explanation: CFCs used in refrigerants and fire extinguishers deplete ozone.
option_feedback: CO₂ causes global warming, not ozone depletion.

questions.question: Which of these is non-biodegradable?
questions.explanation: Polythene is not broken down by decomposers.

options: energy decreases sharply at each step
animals do not like long chains
questions.explanation: Only about 10% passes on, so little energy is left after a few steps.
option_feedback: Decomposers do not limit chain length.
That is not a scientific reason.

questions.question: The UNEP agreement of 1987 aimed to:
questions.explanation: It froze CFC production at 1986 levels.

questions.question: What is a food web? How is it different from a food chain?
answer_steps: A food chain is a single series of organisms, each eating the one before it.
A food web is a network of many interconnected food chains, since one organism is eaten by several others.

questions.question: Why should we use CFC-free refrigerators?
answer_steps: CFCs released from old refrigerators and air conditioners deplete the ozone layer.
A depleted ozone layer lets more harmful UV radiation reach the earth, causing skin cancer and harming living things.

questions.question: State the 10 per cent law. If a plant captures 20 000 J of energy, how much energy will reach a tertiary consumer? Why is the flow of energy called unidirectional?
answer_steps: 10% law: only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level passes on to the next.
20 000 → 2000 (primary) → 200 (secondary) → 20 J (tertiary).
Energy captured by producers does not go back to the Sun, and energy passed to consumers does not return to the lower levels.

questions.question: Distinguish between biodegradable and non-biodegradable substances with two examples each. Why are some substances not biodegradable?
answer_steps: Biodegradable: broken down by decomposers, e.g. vegetable peels, paper.
Non-biodegradable: not broken down by biological processes, e.g. plastic, glass.
Enzymes of microbes are specific, so they cannot act on many synthetic materials.

questions.question: What is the ozone layer? How is ozone formed? How is it being depleted, and what steps have been taken to protect it?
answer_steps: The ozone layer is a layer of ozone (O₃) high in the atmosphere that shields the earth from harmful UV radiation.
UV radiation splits oxygen molecules: $\mathrm{O_{2} \rightarrow O + O}$
Oxygen atoms combine with oxygen molecules: $\mathrm{O + O_{2} \rightarrow O_{3}}$
Synthetic chemicals such as CFCs, used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers, deplete the ozone layer.
In 1987 UNEP forged an agreement to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels; CFC-free refrigerators are now mandatory.

questions.question: Explain, with a food chain, how energy flows through an ecosystem and how pesticides become concentrated. Why should humans be most concerned?
answer_steps: Food chain: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle.
Producers capture about 1% of sunlight; at each step only about 10% of the energy passes on, the rest being used and lost as heat.
So energy decreases sharply up the chain, and chains are short.
Non-degradable pesticides are not broken down, so their concentration increases at each level (biological magnification).
Humans are at the top of many food chains, so the highest concentrations collect in our bodies.

questions.question:
Farmers near a lake sprayed a pesticide on their crops. A few years later, scientists found traces of it in the lake water, much more in the fish, and the highest amount in fish-eating birds, whose eggshells had become thin.

(i) Name the process shown in the case. (1)

(ii) Which organism had the highest concentration of the pesticide? (1)

(iii) Why did the concentration increase along the food chain? OR Suggest two ways to reduce our intake of pesticides. (2)
answer_steps: (i) Biological magnification.
(ii) The fish-eating birds.

(iii) The pesticide is not broken down in the body; each organism eats many organisms from the level below, so the chemical accumulates and its concentration rises at each step. OR Wash fruits and vegetables well before use; prefer organically grown food and support reduced pesticide use.

questions.question:
A school started separating its garbage into green bins (wet waste) and blue bins (dry waste). The green-bin waste was turned into compost for the school garden, and the dry waste was sent for recycling.

(i) Give two examples of waste that should go into the green bin. (1)

(ii) Is plastic biodegradable? (1)

(iii) How does composting help the environment? OR Give two problems caused if dry waste such as plastic is burnt or dumped. (2)
answer_steps: (i) Vegetable and fruit peels, leftover food (any two biodegradable items).
(ii) No, plastic is non-biodegradable.

(iii) Composting turns biodegradable waste into manure that enriches the soil, and reduces the garbage sent to landfills. OR Burning plastic releases harmful gases that pollute the air; dumped plastic pollutes soil and water and harms animals.
